items.title: Frank Netto Interview, 1986-11-10
items.q: He related to Buttsy? Yeah, Buttsy's brother. And, uh, in fact, he was a hell of a lot better saxophone player than Buttsy was a drummer... Buttsy wasn't the greatest drummer in the world, but he was a gentleman. Yeah, that's, yeah, that's right. He was a gentleman.

ctx.x: That was about, oh, I guess about six months or seven months before we broke up. And then we put Steve Massico. You remember Steve Massico? Man, Steve played pretty good. He honked it out real good. He had a good beat and everything else. But he was such a trifling. I said, Richard Gooden. Time to get on the bandstand. We didn't play, but about four choruses, three tunes. And then you'd take 20 minutes off. You couldn't find him at the end of 20 minutes. He related to Buttsy? Yeah, Buttsy's brother. And, uh, in…
Buttsy wasn't the greatest drummer in the world, but he was a gentleman.
